purpose: Define temporary elevation as an explicit bounded authorization state/profile rather than a hidden side effect of stronger authentication.

topics.name: Privilege Elevation Boundary
topics.purpose: Define temporary elevation as an explicit bounded authorization state/profile rather than a hidden side effect of stronger authentication.

semantics.identity_rule: Temporary elevation, if supported, has an explicit grant/evidence identity.
semantics.assurance_rule: Higher assurance may be prerequisite but never sole source of elevated rights.
semantics.lifetime_rule: Elevation lifetime is explicit and bounded.
semantics.revocation_rule: Elevation can be revoked independently from session authentication.
semantics.nonexpansion_rule: Elevation cannot exceed its exact authorized grant.

invariants.rule: Identity, authentication assurance, authorization policy, authorization decision, delegation and runtime execution remain separate machine-significant identities/evidence; no one layer silently substitutes for another.

Ambiguous, missing, stale or unverifiable authority for a protected effect fails closed rather than inheriting trust from locality, transport reachability, process ownership, UI visibility or previous success.

hard_gates.condition: elevation hidden in session flag without identity
logout required as only revocation mechanism

references.purpose: Elevation changes authorization inputs through explicit grant semantics.
